history.period: Trust registered 1976; exact founding date UNVERIFIED
history.summary: A Hindu temple in the heart of Barnala, run by the Om Sat Sanatan Geeta Bhawan Trust, which has held 12AA charitable registration since 1 March 1976 (per the ITAT Chandigarh order in the trust's 80G appeal). The temple's own social-media description calls it an ancient mandir offering daily bhajan, kirtan and arti, providing shelter for sadhus and serving as a spiritual hub for the local community. The central deity is Lord Krishna, with smaller shrines dedicated to Shiva, Durga and Hanuman (source-reported); a school visit report notes the temple's prominent depictions of Lord Ganesha's stories. One travel site claims a 1951 establishment, but no reliable source confirms a founding date — the founding date is UNVERIFIED.

name: Geeta Bhawan
town_description: Barnala is a city and district headquarters in the Malwa region of Punjab, surrounded by Ludhiana, Moga, Mansa, Sangrur and Bathinda districts. It is primarily an agricultural trading town, with the historic Handiaya nearby. The city hosts several Hindu temples, Sikh gurdwaras and Jain temples serving its predominantly Punjabi population.

travel.airport: Nearest domestic airports are Ludhiana (~70 km) (verify); Chandigarh International Airport ~140 km.
travel.railway: Barnala railway station is within the town, on the Ludhiana–Dhuri line.
travel.road: Well connected by road, including NH-7; local buses and autos ply within the city.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, when Punjab's weather is pleasant; Janmashtami and Diwali draw the largest crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open daily with morning and evening aarti; bhajan and kirtan held regularly. Exact daily timings not published (verify).
